headline: Commission finds 32 Cherry Street and 240 Beaver Street gray building not preferably preserved; approves fiberglass gutters for Wellington House and supports Corn Lab rehabilitation CPC application
summary: The commission held demolition delay hearings for 32 Cherry Street and 240 Beaver Street, finding both not preferably preserved. It approved a development prospectus for 96 Tower Road, approved fiberglass replacement gutters for Wellington House, and voted to accept rehabilitation plans and write a letter of support for a CPC application for the 240 Beaver Street Corn Lab.
decisions: Postponed approval of the June 2026 meeting minutes until next month.
Found the house at 32 Cherry Street not preferably preserved.
Approved taking item 6 out of order.
Found the gray building at 240 Beaver Street not preferably preserved.
Approved taking the Corn Lab at 240 Beaver Street rehabilitation item out of order.
Found the 96 Tower Road site, within the 1265 Main Street complex, not historically significant.
Approved use of fiberglass replacement gutters on Wellington House.
Accepted the 240 Beaver Street Corn Lab rehabilitation plans and agreed to write a letter of support for the CPC application, about $37,000, if plans do not change.

plain_text:
Page 1 of 6 
 
Waltham Historical Commission 
Meeting Minutes 
Meeting Date: July 13, 2026, 7:00 PM 
Location: Remote meeting using Zoom 
 
 
1. Chair: Called Meeting to Order at 7:00 PM. 
 
 
2. Secretary: Made the call of the roll 
      
      Commissioner Isaacson, present 
      Commissioner Daly, present 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Dufromont, present 
      Commissioner Egirous, present 
      Commissioner Russo, present 
      Commissioner Wilson, present 
 
       
3. Chair: Reading & Acceptance of the June 2026 Meeting Minutes 
 
Commissioner Russo requested a review of when Commissioner Migdal left the meeting, and 
which votes she participated in. 
 
Commissioner Daly moved to postpone approval of the minutes until next month. 
Commissioner Russo seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
            Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
 
4.   Chair: Announcements: 
 
The FY2027 budget was officially approved by both the Mayor and City Council.  
 
The Boston Globe opinion section included a piece from former Historical Commission 
Chairman Alex Green.
Page 2 of 6 
 
 
Chair: Reading and Description of Correspondence: None 
  
    
5.   Chair: Public Hearings: 
 
Demolition Delay Hearings: 
 
32 Cherry Street 
 
Silvestre Buscemi, the current homeowner, represented the property. The house was built in 
1881 by Sheldon Owen. Residents included employees of the Waltham Watch Factory. 
Neighboring houses are listed on the National Register of Historic Places. A later owner, 
Edward Day Baker, was a prominent figure in Massachusetts in the 1920s and worked with 
Thomas Edison. In later years it became a boarding house. Commissioner Isaacson noted that 
the historic streetscape was a factor in deliberations, and there was discussion of that. Mr. 
Buscemi said that he planned to sell the house and would not oversee what the future owners 
might build there.  
 
Commissioner Daly moved to find the house NOT preferably preserved. 
Commissioner Egirous seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, no 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, no 
            Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
 
Commissioner Daly moved to take item 6 out of order. 
Commissioner Dufromont seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent
Page 3 of 6 
 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
            Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
 
240 Beaver Street (Gray building only) 
 
Jon Millian represented the property on behalf of the City of Waltham. This building was 
used for research at the former UMass Field Station Farm but has since fallen into disrepair. 
The City planned to turn it into a parking lot. Although the building is historic, Chairman 
Isaacson felt there was little chance to save the building. He suggested that the City place a 
historic marker in front of it. Jon Millian agreed.  
 
Commissioner Egirous moved to find the house NOT preferably preserved. 
Commissioner Wilson seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
            Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
 
Commissioner Dufromont moved to take the Corn Lab at 240 Beaver Street 
rehabilitation out of order. 
Commissioner Daly seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
            Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried.
Page 4 of 6 
 
 
 
 
 
6.   Development Prospectus Reviews:  
 
96 Tower Road (within the 1265 Main Street complex) 
 
Mike Connors represented the property on behalf of Sweetgreen LLC. This is the same 
building that will house Cava, which appeared before the historical commission last month. 
 
Commissioner Russo moved to find the site not historically significant. 
Commissioner Daly seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
      Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
 
7.   Stonehurst: Monthly report, including inventory update, Stonehurst Curator: 
 
      No report submitted 
 
 
8.  Wellington House: Monthly Report & Update:  
 
The first floor was reinforced with Lally columns in the basement. Photos were shared. The 
windows were brough to a workshop to be restored. The floor will be refinished. There was 
discussion of replacement materials for the gutters. Jon Millian recommended fiberglass 
gutters rather than wooden ones for better preservation and less maintenance. 
 
Commissioner Dufromont moved to approve the use of fiber glass replacement gutters 
on Wellington House. 
Commissioner Wilson seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes
Page 5 of 6 
 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
      Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
 
9.   Liaison & Subcommittee Reports:  
 
Fernald: A presentation was given to the City Council about moving the Department of 
Public Works to the Fernald property. Chairman Isaacson shared a copy of the presentation 
and pointed out that some historic buildings will likely be demolished as part of this project, 
although there was no mention of demolition in the presentation. There was a brief 
discussion on the project.  
 
Community Preservation Committee (CPC): The First Lutheran Church withdrew their 
application.  
 
Historic Inventory: None 
 
Edu. & Outreach: Reprinting the Watch Factory brochures should be considered at the next 
meeting. 
 
 
10. Old Business: None 
 
 
11. New Business:  
 
Jon Millian wanted to discuss an upcoming CPC application for rehabilitation of the 240 
Beaver Street Corn Lab. This building was used by UMass to research corn. Photos were 
shared. Jon gave an overview of the plans to rehabilitate the building. He planned to prepare 
a CPC application for roughly $37,000. Jon will submit the application to the historical 
commission when it is prepared. 
 
Commissioner Russo moved to accept the rehabilitation plans as presented, and to 
write a letter of support for the application as long as the plans have not changed. 
Commissioner Daly seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes
Page 6 of 6 
 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
      Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
      The motion carried. 
 
Commissioner Egirous asked Jon Millian for an update on Arrigo Farm. Jon said that the 
interior and the barn are still on the list to be renovated but nothing has been scheduled. 
 
 
12. Adjournment: 
 
Commissioner Daly moved to adjourn.  
Commissioner Dufromont seconded. 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, yes 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
      Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:51 PM. 
 
For a recording of the full meeting, please see www.wcac.org
